title: Referrals and Authorizations Extension Arithmetic: Days Added and Span Moved
content:
Under **Referrals and Authorizations**, when the requesting or servicing provider asks to extend an approved authorization of a type that allows extensions, each extension moves the span's last day out by the type's extension validity days and adds days to the authorization.

## Computation

1. **New last day.** The new last day of the span is the current last day plus the type's extension validity days.
2. **Block.** The days an extension adds are the extension's block, which is the type's extension units.
3. **Room under the maximum.** The room left is the type's maximum units per authorization less the units granted and less the units added by earlier extensions, read from the authorization's unit history (its grant entries and extension entries). Units used do not enter the room.
4. **Days added.** The extension adds its days, never more than the room left under the maximum, never fewer than zero, and nothing once the authorization has had the type's maximum extensions (its count of extension entries has reached the type's most extensions).

## Worked example (hypothetical; a type with 14 extension units, 14 extension validity days, a 98-unit maximum and at most 6 extensions)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Units granted | 14 |
| Units added by earlier extensions | 70 (5 extensions) |
| Current last span day | 15 July |

Room left: 98 less 14 less 70, that is 14. The block is 14 days, not more than the room, so 14 days are added and the last span day moves to 29 July. This is the sixth extension; after it the authorization has had 6 extensions and a further request adds nothing.

## Second example (hypothetical)

On a type with 30 extension units, a 120-unit maximum and at most 3 extensions, an authorization with 100 units granted and no earlier extension has a room of 20 left, so an extension adds 20 units, not 30. On the type of the first example, an authorization that has already had 6 extensions gains nothing from a further extension.
